title: Account Boundary Classifier for Dynamic Compliance Pathing
creator: Samantha Lee
description:
Problem: Incoming customer security and compliance requests (SOC2/ISO, HIPAA, GDPR/DPA, vendor questionnaires) currently funnel into a single backlog lane. This causes inconsistent routing to Security/Legal, long SLA slips for enterprise deals, and repeated manual reclassification.

Goal: Build an account-boundary classifier service and routing ruleset that ingests intake data + account metadata and emits a prioritized compliance path (fast-path, legal-review, DPA-exception, on-prem escalation). The classifier should: 1) surface a recommended lane and SLA, 2) attach required evidence templates, and 3) mark cases for automated responses where safe.

Scope: MVP will support SOC2/ISO, DPA/GDPR flagging, and vendor questionnaire triage. HIPAA and industry-specific controls will be handled in follow-up iteration.

Success metrics (MVP):
- Median first-response time for enterprise compliance asks reduced from 6 business days to <= 2 business days for fast-path lanes.
- Manual re-routes reduced by 60%.
- % of inbound asks auto-classified with confidence >= 0.85 (target 70%).

Out of scope: Full automated answer generation for questionnaires, migration of existing backlog items (handled by a separate cleanup ticket).

Acceptance criteria:
- Classifier endpoint deployed to staging and wired into compliance intake workflow.
- Rulebook UI in Console shows classifier decision and signals used.
- Alerting for low-confidence predictions routes to human reviewer.
- Integration tests validate DPA-exempt path and SOC2 fast-path routing.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Kickoff: Reviewed intake pain points with Security and Legal. Agreed to conservative initial rules to avoid false auto-responses. Action: Eng to prototype classifier using existing intake fields + account metadata (region, hosting mode, contract tier). - Samantha Lee

2026-02-20 - Data discovery update: Found that 42% of incoming forms include explicit hosting_mode and 18% contain contract_tier; fallback to NLP on free-text where missing. Data team will provide 6 months of historical intake CSV. - Miguel Ortiz

2026-02-24 - Architecture sync: Decided on a two-stage flow: lightweight rule engine (deterministic) + ML classifier for ambiguous cases. Deterministic rules apply first (e.g., HIPAA flagged by product tag -> legal-review). ML model only used when deterministic confidence is low. - Daniel Kim (Eng Lead)

2026-02-26 - PRD updated with rollout strategy: canary 10% of new requests -> monitor re-route rate and false-positive auto-responses. Added requirement for manual override in Console. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/enterprise/compliance/account-boundary-classifier (internal). - Samantha Lee

2026-02-28 - Design review: UX team submitted wireframes for Rulebook UI and manual override. Feedback: show confidence band, contributing signals, and quick evidence checklist. Design artifact: https://drive.redwood.ai/designs/compliance-rulebook_v1.png - Aisha Patel (Design)

2026-03-01 - Eng update: Staging endpoint deployed, deterministic ruleset running against last 30 days of intake in feature-branch. Initial ML prototype trained on 4k labeled cases reached 0.78 F1. Next steps: tune features (account_age, hosting_mode, contract_tier, prior_asks). GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compliance-classifier/pull/214 - Miguel Ortiz
